messages:
marco: Heads up — after the kernel-mix rollout at 14:00 we saw a pretty reproducible p99 jump on the long-seq workload. p50 unchanged, p95 +10ms, p99 +120ms. GPU util is ~92% during the spike. microbatch=4 on that pool.

lina: Can you paste the short profiler output (kernel timeline + kv hit stats)? wondering if it's a kernel-switch stall or KV miss amplification.

marco: Quick paste from the canary run:
```
seq_len>512: kernel=flash_attn_v2 then fallback=matmul_fast at tail; switch latency ~6ms; kv_hit_rate=0.72; tail window shows batching delay ~8ms
gpu_util: steady 92% before spike, bursts to 98% during tail
```
Looks like kernel handoff + batching alignment causing micro-pauses that blow up tail.

ashok: That matches a saturation cliff: when util hits ~90% the kernel switch path can't amortize the microbatching headroom. Two knobs: lower microbatch (2) to reduce alignment waits, or increase headroom (target util 75–80%). Both reduce throughput.

katie: We should test KV prefetch/warmup too — a 0.72 hit rate means a lot of KV misses are causing extra memory transfers. Try prefetch-first-token and `kv_cache.warmup=true` for a subset. Might smooth the latency without changing microbatching.

marco: Note: regression only shows up for seq>=512 and quantized kernels (q4_0 path). seq<512 unaffected. Possibly kernel selection heuristic is choosing flash for >512 but falls back to matmul for some shapes which stalls.

infra-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T14:00:12 by @deploy-bot: kernel-mix v3 -> canary(5%). Canary healthy: 5m ok, but recent metric drift flagged.

lina: Proposed quick experiments (low-effort):
1) microbatch=2 on canary (5% traffic) + observe p99 for 30m
2) enable kv_prefetch on canary for 5%
3) A/B canary: kernel-mix v3 vs v2 with soft-admit enabled
use `run-profile --tag=canary-kv-prefetch` and capture `p50/p95/p99, gpu_util, kv_hit`

ashok: Also propose soft admission: if gpu.util > 85% then start dropping low-priority requests (5% shed) and avoid starting new ephemeral kernels when residual queue depth>xx. This buys headroom without halving throughput. Simple rule: soft_admit_threshold=0.85, soft_shed_fraction=0.05.

katie: +1 schedule a synthetic load test for seq=512/1024 with 20% traffic shift and add tracing for kernel switch counts. We need timeline traces, not just aggregates. Can someone own the test run? :eyes:

marco: I'll run experiment 1 and 2 now and share profiles. Action items:
- marco: microbatch=2 canary + kv_prefetch experiment (30m)
- lina: prepare traces + agg script to compute kernel-switch rate per 10s window
- ashok: prototype soft_admit rule in simulation env and share config
- katie: schedule synthetic load test for tomorrow and add canary routing (10%)

katie: Cool — if the microbatch=2 recovers p99 but throughput drops <8% we can consider dynamic microbatching: prefer 4 at low util, drop to 2 when util>80%.

marco: Will post raw profile IDs when done: `profile://canary/2065301234/run1`

lina: Thanks — keep posts short, just numbers and trace links. If soft-admit works in sim we can flip on a 10% rollout. :thumbsup:

ashok: One more note: watch for regression in cost-per-token when switching microbatch; if cost jumps too much we might prefer kernel tweaks + kv improvements instead of microbatch shrink.

marco: Updated results (after 30m): microbatch=2 cut p99 from +120ms -> +25ms, throughput -6%, kv_prefetch improved kv_hit to 0.89 and reduced switch events by ~40%. Uploading traces now.

katie: Great data. Next step: run soft_admit sim + A/B on production canary. If sim holds, roll to 10% with monitoring playbook.

infra-bot: Incident alert suppression: playbook 'p99-tail' will be muted for the canary rollout window.

marco: Thanks all. Will post trace links + exact perf numbers in 15m.
